spine_row.acip: ,SROG GCOD PA NI BSAMS BZHIN DU, ,MA NOR BAR NI GZHAN GSAD PA'O, ,MA BYIN LEN PA GZHAN GYI NOR, ,GATHU DANG 'JAB BUS BDAG GIR BYED,
spine_row.wylie: srog gcod pa ni bsams bzhin du, ,ma nor bar ni gzhan gsad pa'o, ,ma byin len pa gzhan gyi nor, ,gathu dang 'jab bus bdag gir byed
spine_row.english: Taking life is killing another being Purposely, and without a mistake. Stealing is to take possession of Another's wealth by means of force or stealth. "What," one may ask, "is the basic nature of each of the ten non-virtues?" (1) The taking of life is defined as killing another being purposely, and without a mistake.  The word "purposely" is meant to indicate that there is no fault where the being in question has died but there was no intent. The words "without a mistake" are meant to indicate that no "actual-commission" stage of an act occurs in a case of mistaken identity; for example, in a case where you undertake to kill Devadatta but instead kill Yajana because you have mistaken him for Devadatta.  The word "another," finally, is meant to indicate that no "actual-commission" stage occurs either in an instance where one takes his own life. (2) Stealing is to take possession of another's wealth, purposely and without a mistake, whether it be by means of superior force of by stealth-                -undetected.
